newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi military ruler invited to OAU summit.
newsitem.headline: Burundi military ruler invited to OAU summit.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) has invited Burundi's military ruler Pierre Buyoya to its summit in Harare in June, his spokesman said on Thursday.
"He received the invitation and he is going," said Sebastian Nahunga, spokesman for the Tutsi military ruler who seized power from Burundi's Hutu civilian president in a coup last July.
"Without doubt he will participate as president of the Republic of Burundi. That is the meaning of this invitation."
Nahunga said Buyoya would raise at the annual OAU summit regional sanctions against Burundi imposed shortly after the coup and his goal was for them to be lifted entirely.
The regional leaders eased sanctions against Burundi last month and invited Buyoya to their summit in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha, where he was addressed as president.
Nahunga said Buyoya wanted support at the OAU meeting from June 2 to 4 for his government's talks with the main Hutu rebel group, the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD).
Buyoya announced last week his government had secret talks with the CNDD in Italy. The move has been met by opposition from some Tutsis, who accuse the Hutus of being genocidal killers.
"We need the support of the continent, of other African countries, and the international community," Nahunga said.

Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army arrested 14 students on Wednesday during a university sit-in protest against Buyoya's decision to negotiate with the rebels. Both sides signed a pre-ceasefire agreement after their secret talks in Rome.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi in massacres and civil war since October 1993, when the country's first elected Hutu president was murdered by Tutsi troops.
